# Lair of the Troll King

*Page PDF 37*

THE TROLL COUNTRY 

## **The Bay of Blades**
The Bay of Blades is named for the many sharks circling its waters, including the beautiful Norscan Blue and fierce Grey Barbed. A heavy shingle beach surrounds the bay, and a waterfall drops from the cliffs above, carving a gouge to the sea. The waterfall makes the Bay a convenient place for ships to take on fresh water. Lumps of strange green amber are sometimes found here, washed down from mountain forests. 

Carved into the cliffs on either side of the Bay are two caves, one containing a shrine to Neiglen (as Nurgle is known by the Sarl), the other to Mermedus. Eremites of both or either god may be present, though the cults are not entirely friendly and they usually treat each other with chilly disdain. They offer foretellings or the sacred signs of their god in return for tribute. 

The Bay is sacred to the Sarl and Skaeling as a place to settle disputes without resorting to full-scale war. Two aggrieved vessels sail alongside one another. Blood and offal are slopped into the water to attract sharks. Then a sturdy plank is laid between the two vessels. The contending parties stand upon the plank and fight. Aside from natural weapons, only an axe and length of knotted rope are permitted. Only one fighter is allowed to return to their ship. It’s a lesser-known fact that outsiders can demand this contest of a pirate captain, perhaps to gain their freedom after capture. In this case, an agreeable second ship must be found to assist the ritual. 

## **Lair of the Troll King**
Like Throgg himself, it’s hard to tell where stories end and truth begins with regard to the Troll King’s lair. It’s agreed that Throgg resides in the far north-east of Troll Country, close to the icy estuary leading into Aesling lands. Beyond that, details are uncertain. A fortress of ice, a gigantic archway in a mountainside, a bottomless pit in a forest: all are offered as places to seek. Thereafter it’s said that Throgg’s quartz throne sits at the heart of a frozen labyrinth, from the walls of which project the frozen limbs and heads of half-chewed victims, princes and paupers alike. An army of foul beasts stalk its tunnels, threatening all who venture within. So say the storytellers. 

Stories are spiced with rumours and temptations: imprisoned Norse princes and princesses, shivering in animal furs, whose families offer rich rewards for their rescue; caverns filled with booty taken from ambushed Norse pirates and Troll Country nomads; wizards and shamans captured and forced to experiment with magics to turn Trolls from witless beasts into thoughtful beings. Some say only a throne of diamond could support Throgg’s muscled bulk. 

Thogg’s lair has become a legend even among Troll Slayers, a perfect end for their personal stories. Expeditions are mounted, usually by ship, but the only ones who return are Slayers who fail to find the lair, or sailors and guides who are lucky to return frost-bitten and gibbering.
